summary: Deterministic verdict: PASS for the run-intersection window (1790619855000–1790620200000 ms). The only evaluated policy, overall-errors (error_rate_ratio <= 0.01), observed 0 errors / 36,034 samples and returned PASS (evidence 14, 15). This PASS, however, rests on partial evidence: the OpenSearch errors source query FAILED with SOURCE_HTTP_ERROR after 2 retries (3 requests), making analysis coverage INCOMPLETE (SOURCE_ACQUISITION_PARTIAL) (evidence 16 and facts). The resource verdict is NO_POLICY — no resource threshold was evaluated, which is not a pass (evidence 15). Clock alignment is not verified by core, so temporal/lead-lag hypotheses are unsupported until clock verification (evidence 7). JMeter-derived data show zero errors across 37,349 samples, reported throughput_rps ratio 37,349,000/359,969, overall latency p50/p95/p99/max = 17/98/176/1092 ms, per-transaction p99 from 85 to 197 ms, low and stable per-service CPU/memory (23/23 cells, no gaps), and detected_idle_gaps = 0. Findings list is empty. Advice below does not change the deterministic verdict.

hypotheses.observation: The error-rate policy check passed with observed 0 errors / 36,034 samples (evidence 14), while the OpenSearch 'errors' source query status is FAILED with reason SOURCE_HTTP_ERROR after 3 requests and 2 retries, leaving source status PARTIAL and analysis coverage INCOMPLETE (SOURCE_ACQUISITION_PARTIAL) (evidence 16, analysis_coverage fact).
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Additional error signals that the analysis intended to ingest from the errors source were not acquired; the zero-error picture may be incomplete for the sources planned, rather than proven across all of them.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Retry/re-run the failed OpenSearch 'errors' query, checking index availability, credentials, and the HTTP error cause; then re-confirm the error-rate policy result once coverage becomes COMPLETE.

hypotheses.observation: Overall latency is p50 17 ms, p95 98 ms, p99 176 ms, max 1092 ms (evidence 0); checkout shows p99 142 ms and max 1092 ms (evidence 3). All transactions report error_count 0, and only the error-rate policy (overall-errors) exists (evidence 14).
hypotheses.possible_explanation: A small number of high-latency samples far beyond p99 may indicate occasional slow calls or transient contention, but no latency policy was defined, so these maxima are not classified as pass or fail by any policy.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Extract and inspect the max-latency samples from the JTL and check whether they cluster in time; first verify clock alignment (evidence 7) before correlating with resource series, and consider adding an explicit latency threshold policy if tail latency matters.

hypotheses.observation: Resource summaries show low, stable means with small IQR/MAD and no gaps across 23/23 cells: frontend CPU mean 0.1803007391 cores, checkoutservice CPU mean 0.0469146521 cores, paymentservice CPU mean 0.0111971304 cores; frontend memory mean ~12,059,870 bytes, checkoutservice ~9,282,456 bytes, paymentservice ~33,023,347 bytes (evidence 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13). Resource verdict is NO_POLICY (evidence 15).
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The workload may not be saturating these services, or per-interval aggregation / replica scaling could be masking per-instance load; low observed utilization is not proof of spare capacity, and NO_POLICY means no threshold comparison was made.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Compare observed utilization against replica counts and any autoscaling configuration; add a resource policy with explicit thresholds if capacity headroom needs to be adjudicated, since NO_POLICY currently means no resource pass/fail was determined.

hypotheses.observation: Evaluation window is 1790619855000–1790620200000 ms (345 s) while the run spans 1790619844691–1790620204660 ms; 1 leading cell (10,309 ms) and 1 trailing cell (4,660 ms) were dropped, auto_window_status is DERIVED, and the errors source is FAILED (evidence 7, 16).
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The run edges (potential ramp-up/ramp-down) were trimmed from the evaluated window, and any error signal in those edge intervals from the failed errors source would be unobserved.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Confirm that the edge trimming matches the intended snapshot/index boundaries; consider a fixed evaluation window with explicit margins and a recovered errors source if edge behavior or ramp effects matter.

recommendations.action: Investigate and recover the failed OpenSearch 'errors' source (SOURCE_HTTP_ERROR, 3 requests, 2 retries) and re-run the analysis until coverage is COMPLETE.
recommendations.rationale: The PASS verdict currently relies on an error rate from acquired JMeter/JTL-derived data, while analysis coverage is INCOMPLETE (SOURCE_ACQUISITION_PARTIAL) because the errors source query failed; coverage must be restored before the zero-error result can be relied upon across all planned sources.

recommendations.action: Verify clock alignment between JTL timestamps and Prometheus resource series before performing any time-correlation or lead/lag reasoning.
recommendations.rationale: The resource binding reports clock_alignment = not_verified_by_core, so the relationship between request timestamps and resource series is unverified and cannot support temporal causal hypotheses.

recommendations.action: Add explicit latency and resource policies if latency or capacity are in scope, since only the overall-errors error-rate policy is currently evaluated.
recommendations.rationale: The window policy summary shows business_verdict PASS for error rate only and resource_verdict NO_POLICY; there is no latency threshold and no resource threshold, so p99/p95/max latencies and CPU/memory behavior are not adjudicated by any policy.

recommendations.action: Review whether trimming the run edges (1 leading cell dropped = 10,309 ms; 1 trailing cell dropped = 4,660 ms) excludes meaningful warmup/cooldown behavior from the evaluated window.
recommendations.rationale: The run spans 359,969 ms but the evaluation window is 345,000 ms, with auto window status DERIVED; any events in the trimmed edge intervals are outside the evaluated policy window, and the failed errors source could have hidden edge-window errors.

caveats: Analysis coverage is INCOMPLETE (SOURCE_ACQUISITION_PARTIAL); the OpenSearch 'errors' source query FAILED with SOURCE_HTTP_ERROR after 2 retries, so error signals from that source were not acquired (evidence 16, analysis_coverage fact).
resource_verdict is NO_POLICY: absence of resource policy is not a pass; no resource thresholds were evaluated (evidence 15).
clock_alignment = not_verified_by_core: the clock relationship between request data and resource series is unverified, so no lead/lag ordering or temporal causal hypothesis is supported (evidence 7).
Only the error-rate policy (overall-errors, threshold 0.01) was evaluated; no latency policy exists, so the observed 1092 ms max and per-transaction p99 up to 197 ms are not classified by any policy.
Resource summaries are 15-second interval means (step_ms 15000, observed_cells 23); sub-interval spikes are not represented and flat/low mean series do not prove stability or spare capacity.

detected_idle_gaps = 0 and longest_idle_gap_ms = null only describe the evaluated window; they do not prove sustained activity outside it, and the errors source failure limits idle-gap/error coverage.
throughput_rps values are reported as ratios (numerator/denominator, e.g., 37,349,000/359,969 overall); interpretation is relative to the reported run duration.
The deterministic verdict PASS is preserved unchanged; this advisory does not alter it.
Findings list is empty; no additional anomaly or finding was generated by the core analysis.
